pages.name: understand
pages.title: What is happening inside the chat?

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.intro
elements.html:
Trace a typical cloud-chat request and separate generating a reply from checking a claim.

A chat interface shows a reply; it does not show everything that happened behind it. In this fictional cloud service, a trained model generates text. First trace the journey in your own words. Then compare a claim with dated evidence. You need no external account or live AI tool.

Practice scenario

Fictional club exercise, 13 October 2026. You ask a cloud chat: “When does the club meet this week?” It replies, “Definitely Friday at 4.” No timetable was supplied and no search or source is shown. Route cards, scrambled: A — app displays the returned reply; B — trained model generates output on the service; C — you type the prompt in the app; D — network carries the request to the service, which prepares the input.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.teaching
elements.html:
Follow the message, then the reply

For these cards: C → D → B → A. The app collects your prompt. The network carries it to the service; the service prepares the model input. The trained model generates output. The service sends the reply back over the network, and the app displays it. The interface, network, service and model do different jobs.

Training changes; inference uses

Recall Lesson 2: training adjusts a model using data. Inference uses the trained model. Text models work with tokens—pieces of text—and generate using learned patterns and available context. Producing this reply does not, by itself, mean the model changed or searched the web.

A reply and a source do different jobs

Fluent text can be useful and still be wrong. To check a schedule, inspect evidence from someone responsible for it. Ask: does this source cover this meeting, and has it been updated? A newer unsupported reply is not automatically stronger evidence than an applicable organizer notice.

Trace, compare, revise

  1. Save your own route before opening the worked trace. Use letters or sentences, with a return path.
  2. Compare the model’s Friday claim against both dated notices. Save your explanation before opening the comparison choices.
  3. Use the final book-swap case to write a supported notice and explain one claim you withheld.
  4. Review your reasoning against the criteria. No real personal details or outside account are needed.

Can you explain both how text was generated and why a particular source supports your correction?

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.route
elements.title: Compare with your own trace. Which account fits this cloud service?

choices.text: C → D → B → A. The service uses a trained model; the reply returns over the network.
C → D → B → A. Each reply necessarily retrains the model on this message.
C → D → A → B. The app first retrieves a verified answer; the model then checks it.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.route.feedback.cloud
elements.html: That traces prompt, transport and service, model inference, then the reply. It does not establish a search or fact-check.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.route.feedback.train
elements.html: The travel order fits, but using a trained model is inference. A product may separately use stored data for later training; a reply alone does not establish that.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.route.feedback.search
elements.html: In this scenario the model generates the reply before it is displayed. No search or verification is shown. Revisit what each card actually says.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.predictions
elements.html:
Every card is invented for this exercise. Today in the scenario is 13 October 2026. No model was run. Compare responsibility, date and relevance; the chat has no shown access to either notice.

Fictional source packet: this week’s club meeting
CardSource and dateWhat it says
AClub noticeboard · 5 October 2026Weekly club: Fridays at 16:00, room 4.
BClub organizer update · 12 October 2026This week only: the meeting moves to Thursday 15 October, 16:00, in the library. This replaces the Friday meeting.
CGenerated chat reply · 13 October 2026Definitely Friday at 4. No source or search shown.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.evidence_comparison
elements.title: Compare the Friday claim with both notices. Which source applies to this week, and why? Write a corrected message with its source and one thing the packet does not establish.
elements.description: Self-review: Use dates, source responsibility and which meeting each notice covers.; Explain why “definitely” or repetition does not verify a claim.; State a limit without inventing missing details.. Presence only; not automatically graded.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.verify
elements.title: After your own source comparison, which message is justified by the packet?

choices.text: “For this week, the organizer’s 12 October update says Thursday at 16:00 in the library. I would use that update.”
“Friday at 4 is confirmed: both the older notice and the chat agree.”
“Friday at 4: the 13 October chat reply is newer than both notices.”

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.verify.feedback.source
elements.html: This names both the evidence and its scope. The older notice describes the earlier plan; confident chat wording adds no verification.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.verify.feedback.share
elements.html: Agreement is not enough. Check whether the notice still applies after the organizer’s dated update.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.verify.feedback.latest
elements.html: A newer timestamp does not give a generated reply authority over an organizer’s update. Ask what source knows and whether it covers this week.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.evidence_check
elements.title: The reply repeats Friday. What would change the evidence?

choices.text: Ask for a more confident version of the same reply.
Check the current organizer update, or ask the organizer if the update is unclear.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.evidence_check.feedback.repeat
elements.html: That changes wording, not the source of the timetable.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.evidence_check.feedback.official
elements.html: Use evidence from someone responsible for the schedule and check which meeting it covers.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.transfer
elements.title: New fictional case: a chat says “The book swap definitely has free pizza.” The current organizer card says “Tuesday, library, 15:30–16:00, free entry”; it says nothing about food. Write a notice you would share, identify what you withheld and why, and name a check that could resolve the food claim. Then explain why generating this reply is inference, not proof that the model retrained or searched.
elements.description: Practice text only. Saved on this device. Reviewed by you or an educator, not AI graded.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.rubric
elements.html:
Self-check

  • Notice includes only supported facts; free entry is not a promise of food.
  • Withholds the food claim without claiming food is definitely absent.
  • Names the responsible organizer or an applicable source as a check.
  • Distinguishes inference from training and does not assume search.

This simplified route describes a fictional cloud service. Other products may use on-device models or tools. Chat retention, later training use and search depend on the product and settings. All dates, notices and replies here are invented teaching fixtures; no model was run.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l03.self_review
elements.title: Self-review: identify one change or clarification in your original trace or source comparison. Explain why it matters. What would you check if the organizer issued another update?
elements.description: Self-review: Point to your own words and a specific reason.; Describe what new evidence would change your decision.. Presence only; not automatically graded.
